chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man wishes to marry a woman, so he looks at her hair.' He said, 'Yes, he merely wishes to purchase her at the highest price.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man looking at a woman's hair before marriage?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits a suitor to view his prospective bride’s hair, interpreting the gaze as a commercial assessment of value ('buying her at the highest price'). This reflects the Shia juristic view that such looking is a practical necessity for ensuring compatibility and consent, provided it is done with modesty and for the purpose of marriage rather than mere pleasure.
